title: sp00ky.yml
description: Configuration file for Sp00ky — an offline-first, real-time sync framework built on SurrealDB.

slug.description: Cloud project slug used by `spooky cloud` commands. Must be unique across Sp00ky Cloud.

surrealdb.description: SurrealDB configuration. Can be a version string (e.g. "v3.0.0") or a full config object.

version.description: Sp00ky service versions. A string sets both SSP and Scheduler everywhere. A `{ssp, scheduler}` object splits per service. A `{dev, cloud}` object splits per environment (currently only `dev` is consumed by `spky dev`; `cloud` is reserved). Each service entry may be an image version tag or a `{ path }` object pointing at a host-built binary.

oneOf.description: Version tag applied to both SSP and Scheduler (e.g. "canary", "v1.0.0").
Individual versions for SSP and Scheduler (applies to all envs). Each is an image tag or a `{ path }` to a host-built binary.
Per-environment versions. Currently only `dev` is consumed; `cloud` is reserved.

logLevel.description: `RUST_LOG` directive applied to the Scheduler and SSP containers (both `spky dev` and `spky cloud deploy`). A plain string applies everywhere (e.g. `trace`, `info,ssp=debug`). A `{dev, cloud}` map sets per-environment levels. Unset → defaults to `info`.

oneOf.description: Single `RUST_LOG` directive applied in every environment. Accepts bare levels (`trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `off`) or comma-separated `target=level` pairs.
Per-environment log level. `dev` is consumed by `spky dev`; `cloud` is sent to the cloud control plane on every deploy.

dev.description: RUST_LOG directive used for local `spky dev` containers.

cloud.description: RUST_LOG directive applied to the remote scheduler/SSP after `spky cloud deploy`.

schema.description: Schema directory or explicit paths. A string is treated as the base directory (convention: schema/src/schema.surql, schema/migrations/, schema/src/buckets/).

oneOf.description: Base directory for schema files. Sub-paths are derived by convention.
Explicit paths for schema, migrations, and buckets.

schema.description: Path to the main SurrealQL schema file.

apps.description: Application definitions (backends, frontends, docker). Each key is the app name. A value is either an inline app config, or a reference `{ path: ./dir }` that pulls the app config from `./dir/sp00ky.app.yml` (fields set alongside `path` override the referenced file).

schedules.description: Server-side cron/interval schedules, keyed by name. Each cycle the scheduler creates a new job row in the backend's outbox table. The whole section may instead be a path to a YAML file holding the map.

oneOf.description: Path to a YAML file holding the whole schedules map, relative to the manifest.

workflows.description: Server-side workflow DAGs, keyed by name. Same file-linking rule as `schedules`.

oneOf.description: Path to a YAML file holding the whole workflows map, relative to the manifest.

buckets.description: List of SurrealQL bucket definition files.

cloudApi.description: Override the Sp00ky Cloud API endpoint (e.g. for staging).

refMode.description: Storage layout for the SSP's internal `_00_list_ref` table. 'dedicated' (default) gives each authenticated user their own `_00_list_ref_user_<id>` table; 'single' keeps the legacy shared `_00_list_ref`. Dedicated works around a SurrealDB v3 LIVE-permission gap on permission-gated tables.

anonymousLiveQueries.description: Enable realtime sync for unauthenticated (anonymous) clients. When true, the SSP materializes anonymous query registrations into a world-readable `_00_list_ref_anon` table so logged-out visitors get live updates. Defaults to false (anonymous clients can read one-shot but never sync live).

versionSpec.description: A version tag (string) or `{ssp, scheduler}` object. Used inside per-environment version splits.

serviceVersion.description: A single Sp00ky service version: either an image version tag (string) or a `{ path }` object pointing at a host-built binary (consumed by `spky dev`).

oneOf.description: Run a host-built binary instead of a published image.

path.description: Path to a locally-built binary, relative to sp00ky.yml or absolute (e.g. "../target/debug/ssp-server").

secretValue.description: A literal value, or a reference to an encrypted vault key resolved at deploy time.

vault.description: Vault key name whose decrypted value is used.

hosting.description: Whether SurrealDB is hosted on Sp00ky Cloud or externally.

endpoint.description: SurrealDB endpoint URL (literal or { vault: KEY }). Required when hosting is "external"; not allowed otherwise.

username.description: SurrealDB username (literal or { vault: KEY }). Only valid when hosting is "external". Default "root".

password.description: SurrealDB password (literal or { vault: KEY }). Only valid when hosting is "external". Default "root".

else.description: Credentials are only meaningful for external hosting; the managed DB generates its own root password.

appEntry.description: An app entry. Either a full inline app config (see app.schema.json), or a `{ path }` reference that pulls the app's config from `<path>/sp00ky.app.yml`. Fields set alongside `path` override the referenced file (main overrides sub).

oneOf.description: Reference a service's own config file. `path` points at a directory containing sp00ky.app.yml; any other field set here overrides the referenced file.

path.description: Directory (relative to sp00ky.yml) that contains this app's sp00ky.app.yml.

format.description: Output format. 'typescript' uses the built-in generator; 'dart' runs spooky_core's rich generator (`dart run spooky_core:spooky_gen`) from `workdir`.

output.description: Output file path for the generated types (relative to sp00ky.yml).

workdir.description: For format: dart — optional override for the directory (relative to sp00ky.yml) to run the Dart generator from. Must be a Dart package that depends on spooky_core. By default it's auto-derived from `output`'s nearest ancestor pubspec.yaml. Ignored for TypeScript.

sspCount.description: Number of SSP instances to provision. Overrides the plan default.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the infrastructure containers, keyed by role. Backends read their env from the encrypted vault (`spky env set`); this is the equivalent for the containers Sp00ky Cloud owns. Values are NOT secrets - they are stored unencrypted in the project's cloud config. Keys the control plane manages itself (SPKY_DB_*, SPKY_AUTH_SECRET, SPKY_SSP_ID, SPKY_JOB_CONFIG, S3_*) are refused. Takes effect on the next container creation, so a deploy or restart is required.

storageConfig.description: Persistent bucket storage. When sizeGB is set, buckets use a file backend on a volume mounted at /buckets (path file:/buckets/<name>) instead of memory, and the size provisions an extra disk (dev docker mount + cloud). sizeGB is provisioning size only, not a SurrealDB-enforced quota.

sizeGB.description: GB to allocate for persistent bucket files. A positive value enables the file backend for new buckets and mounts the storage volume.

bucketUrl.description: External S3-compatible bucket URL. If set, MinIO is skipped.

credentialsEnvFile.description: Path to env file with BACKUP_ACCESS_KEY and BACKUP_SECRET_KEY.

forEachConfig.description: Fan out: run this SurrealQL SELECT each fire and spawn one job per row. The row is passed to the handler as `payload.row`.

query.description: A single SurrealQL SELECT statement. Runs with root privileges.

key.description: Row field whose value keys the per-row concurrency check. Defaults to `id`.

strategy.description: Backoff shape, matching the job runner.

retentionConfig.description: How long finished jobs and run history are kept, before they are deleted automatically. Asymmetric by outcome: a success is read once if at all, a failure is what you went looking for. Whatever is deleted is first folded into permanent hourly counters, so totals survive the rows. `pending` and `processing` jobs, and `running` runs, are never pruned at any age.

success.description: How long outbox jobs in `success` are kept, e.g. `6h`. Ages by `updated_at` — a terminal job's last write is its terminalization.

failed.description: How long outbox jobs in `failed` are kept, e.g. `14d`.

runSuccess.description: How long schedule/workflow runs in `success`, `skipped` or `replaced` are kept, e.g. `24h`. Ages by `finished_at`.

runFailed.description: How long schedule/workflow runs in `failed` or `killed` are kept, e.g. `30d`.

maxRows.description: Hard ceiling on rows in a successful status, per table. `0` (the default) disables it. Trims oldest-first and never touches failures — a valve for very wide fan-out, where the age windows above are the main mechanism.

mode.description: Default history mode for every schedule. `failures-only` means a successful execution leaves nothing but a rollup counter. A schedule's own `history:` overrides it either way. Resolved at deploy time, so changing it needs a redeploy — unlike the windows above, which are one UPDATE away. Never applies to client `db.run()` jobs.

historyConfig.description: Per-schedule override of the project's run-history retention. Accepts the shorthand `failures-only` (or `all`) as well as the full object, because "never keep a successful run" is the common answer for a wide fan-out and should not require thinking about durations.

mode.description: `failures-only` never persists a successful run: a suppressed tick writes no row at all, and a clean run is deleted as it finalizes. Counts still land in the rollup.

success.description: How long this schedule's `success` / `skipped` / `replaced` runs are kept, e.g. `15m`. Omitted falls back to the project's `retention.runSuccess`.

failed.description: How long this schedule's `failed` / `killed` runs are kept, e.g. `30d`. Omitted falls back to the project's `retention.runFailed`.

scheduleEntry.description: A server-side schedule: either an inline definition, or a path to a YAML file containing one. Set exactly one of `cron` or `every`. `cron` is a standard 5-field expression evaluated in `timezone` (default UTC); `every` is a fixed interval measured from each fire.

oneOf.description: Path to a YAML file holding this schedule's definition, relative to the manifest.

cron.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (an optional leading seconds field is accepted), e.g. `0 3 * * *`.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the cron expression is evaluated in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Defaults to UTC.

backend.description: Name of an `apps:` entry with an outbox method.

route.description: Route path on that backend, e.g. `/syncGames`.

payload.description: Static payload merged into every spawned job's payload.

concurrency.description: What happens when a fire lands while the previous run for the same key is still going. `skip` records the suppressed tick and leaves the in-flight run alone; `allow` permits overlap; `replace` kills the in-flight run first.

timeout.description: Per-job HTTP timeout, e.g. `120s`. Honoured only when the backend sets `deploy.timeoutOverridable`.

enabled.description: `false` deploys the schedule but leaves it inert. Distinct from `spky schedules pause`, which config never overwrites.

backend.description: Name of an `apps:` entry with an outbox method.

dependsOn.description: Steps that must succeed first. A step with none is a root and runs in parallel with the other roots; a step with several is a fan-in join.

workflowEntry.description: A workflow DAG: either an inline definition, or a path to a YAML file containing one.

oneOf.description: Path to a YAML file holding this workflow's definition, relative to the manifest.

schedule.description: When to run it. Omit for a trigger-only workflow. Set exactly one of `cron` or `every`. `cron` is a standard 5-field expression evaluated in `timezone` (default UTC); `every` is a fixed interval measured from each fire.

steps.description: Steps by name. Order is irrelevant — `dependsOn` decides execution.

onFailure.description: `halt` fails the run and skips every step that hasn't started; `continue-independent` skips only the branch below the failure. Either way the run ends failed.

concurrency.description: What happens when a fire lands while the previous run for the same key is still going. `skip` records the suppressed tick and leaves the in-flight run alone; `allow` permits overlap; `replace` kills the in-flight run first.
